title: dedicated: Add burst queueing, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting to fleet autoscaler
author: Aisha Kumar
description: This PR extends the Dedicated fleet autoscaler with three customer-facing and operational capabilities: 1) burst queueing via a token-bucket-backed credit pool so short traffic spikes can be absorbed without immediate scale-up, 2) throughput guarantees that let fleet owners set a per-fleet minimum tokens/sec SLO and a preferred scaling curve to meet steady-state throughput, and 3) utilization and burst consumption reporting surfaced through metrics and the Console. Motivation: customers expect predictable latency/cost under transient load and operators need visibility into how burst credits are consumed and when fleets hit throughput floors. Implementation: - Introduce a new AutoscalerPolicy CRD fields: burst_credit_rate, burst_bucket_size, min_throughput_rps, throughput_scale_curve. - Implement token-bucket allocator in the autoscaler runtime with optimistic queueing: when credits exist requests are queued on the fleet for up to 250ms, otherwise autoscaler triggers scale decisions using the new throughput SLO path. - Add per-fleet metrics: redwood.dedicated.fleet.utilization, redwood.dedicated.fleet.burst_credits_remaining, redwood.dedicated.fleet.burst_consumption_rate, and redwood.dedicated.fleet.throughput_guarantee_violations. Metrics are tagged with fleet_id and region. - Console changes: new fleet-level pane showing current credit balance, recent consumption histogram, and throughput-SLO health. - Backward compatibility: existing autoscaler configs default to previous behavior (burst_credit_rate=0, min_throughput_rps unset) so no rollout work necessary for fleets not opting in. Rollout: staged rollout behind feature flag dedicated.fleet.burst_queueing with Canary on 5% of new fleets, followed by 25% then global. Testing: unit tests for token-bucket logic, integration tests simulating spike patterns, and a perf canary that validates no regression in median latency under steady load. Checklist: - [x] CRD + validation schema - [x] Autoscaler runtime implementation - [x] Metrics + exporter - [x] Console UI - [x] E2E tests - [x] Docs updated (internal + public) Related: Linear ENG-1963 (autoscaler refactor), ENG-2147 (console fleet UI), SUP-4521 (customer incident motivating burst control).
commits: Add AutoscalerPolicy fields for burst and throughput guarantees
Implement token-bucket allocator and optimistic queueing in autoscaler runtime
Expose burst and throughput metrics via metrics-exporter and Prometheus
Add Console fleet pane and API endpoints for credit queries
Add unit and integration tests for burst behavior
Docs: explain burst controls and SLO fields
review_conversation: Marco Silva: Please add invariants around credit accumulation when fleet is at max_size (otherwise credits could grow unbounded).
Aisha Kumar: Added cap enforcement in token_bucket.go and unit tests covering max_size behavior.

Linnea Park: Need a prometheus-friendly metric name for burst consumption — prefer redwood_dedicated_fleet_burst_consumption_rate. Updated exporter to export both dotted and snake_case names for compatibility.
Ethan Nguyen: Confirmed no regression in steady-state median latency in perf canary. Approving.
release_notes: Added burst queueing and throughput guarantees to Dedicated fleet autoscaler. New policy fields allow operators to configure burst credit rates and minimum throughput SLOs. Console now reports fleet-level credit balance and consumption metrics. Backward compatible by default.
notes_for_ops: Feature enabled behind feature flag dedicated.fleet.burst_queueing. Rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Monitor redwood.dedicated.fleet.throughput_guarantee_violations and redwood.dedicated.fleet.burst_credits_remaining during rollout. If excessive queueing (>250ms) is observed, disable feature and investigate credit rates vs traffic profiles.
